t: This is Thurloe Square, a traditional garden square in South Kensington. It takes its name from John Thurloe, a barrister who served as secretary to the council of state under the Protectorate, and was spymaster for Oliver Cromwell. Others have a connection here too. Edward Douglas-Scott-Montagu, later the third Baron Montagu of Beaulieu, was born in the square. He went on to found the National Motor Museum. The hospital administrator Sir Mark Baring lived here, and the railway engineer and botanical collector Hastings Charles Dent was born here.
